messages:
tess: Ran into a console UX edge: p95 timeline for service:autocomplete is showing periodic spikes only in the rollup view. Endpoint p95 is smooth. Could be shard TTL mismatch.

alejandro: Timeline spikes but endpoint steady usually means one shard injected a delayed batch. Do we have any retention TTL differences between the rolling aggregator and endpoint snapshots?

maria: Aggregator keeps a 5m flush window; endpoint-level stream uses near-realtime. If a late shard arrives it can create a spike in aggregated windows that the endpoint view (which filters late arrivals) doesn't.

jamal: We could tag late-arrival contributions and mark rollup points as "partial" until all expected shards report. But that adds complexity to ingestion (track expected contributors).

oncall-jen: Hotfix idea: if a rollup point sees a sudden sample_count delta > 500 in 10s, mark it flagged and expose an explanation in console tooltip.

tess: That helps, but UX wants persistence: product asks for a legend item: "data completeness warnings". Also want the ability to hide rollup anomalies when viewing SLO windows.

alejandro: Short-term: add a small amber triangle on the chart when flagged. Long-term: we should harmonize flush windows or make endpoint and rollup align to the same event-time windowing.

maria: Note: changing flush window might increase throughput/backpressure on aggregator. We need to measure.

jamal: I'll prototype the delta-detection flag in aggregator this week and add a simple boolean in metadata. Then the console can render the triangle and tooltip linking to runbook.

oncall-jen: I'll watch the canary and validate flagged events correlate with ingress-late arrivals.

-- end of thread --
